purpose: Research-only direct ADHD/bullying–substance-use source expansion; no clinical release or individual-risk inference
eligibility_rule: PubMed ID, publication within 20 years as of appraisal, direct ADHD or bullying/peer-victimization exposure and substance-use outcome, no known retraction on the inspected PubMed record
method: Design-matched bounded-use appraisal of full article text and PubMed records, considering selection, measurement, temporality, confounding, analysis and transportability. This is not a numeric quality score. Full-text access route is recorded per item. Independent item-by-item quality adjudication remains outstanding.
source_representation_if_approved: PubMed abstract and metadata only, consistent with the existing Qdrant corpus; no article full text is licensed or queued for indexing.
admission_gate: Silpa explicitly approved adding the five named PubMed papers to the research-only Qdrant corpus on 2026-09-25. The binary bounded-use appraisal gate passed for research ingestion only; human item-by-item quality adjudication and clinical release remain outstanding.

human_approval.scope: Add these five PMIDs to the existing research-only Qdrant corpus for the stated bounded uses
human_approval.basis: Project conversation: 'add the 5 papers to qdrant as well, i approve the pubmeds'

candidates.title: Prospective association of childhood ADHD and substance use and abuse/dependence: a meta-analytic review
candidates.text_reviewed: Complete 14-page author-hosted PDF and PubMed record; text extracted with pypdf
candidates.bounded_use: Prospective-study synthesis reports greater subsequent nicotine and other-substance use and nicotine, alcohol, marijuana, cocaine and other abuse/dependence outcomes among children with ADHD; ever-use of alcohol was not significantly higher. Do not assert an ADHD-specific causal effect.
candidates.strength: Twenty-seven eligible prospective studies and 65 effect sizes; predefined inclusion criteria, random-effects pooling, heterogeneity and publication-bias checks, and substance-specific use versus disorder outcomes.
candidates.critical_limit: Comorbid disruptive behavior disorders could partly or wholly account for associations and were not formally meta-analyzed; treatment and other psychiatric comorbidity were also not resolved. Older studies and binary lifetime outcomes limit present-day and individual application. Publication-bias tests with few studies per outcome do not rule out missing evidence.

candidates.title: Substance use through adolescence into early adulthood after childhood-diagnosed ADHD: findings from the MTA longitudinal study
candidates.outcome: substance-use onset, frequency and escalation, not incident SUD
candidates.text_reviewed: PMC author-manuscript full text and PubMed record
candidates.bounded_use: In the MTA comparison, childhood ADHD was associated with earlier use and higher young-adult weekly marijuana use and daily cigarette smoking; do not translate frequency into diagnosed SUD or assert that every substance category increased in adulthood.
candidates.strength: Rigorous childhood diagnosis, classmates as comparison, and repeated substance-use questionnaires through mean age 25.
candidates.critical_limit: Observational follow-up of a treatment trial, self-reported substance use, possible attrition and comorbid/exposure confounding, and combined-type ADHD enrollment limit causal and population-wide claims.

candidates.title: Peer Victimization, Depressive Symptoms, and Substance Use: A Longitudinal Analysis
candidates.exposure: peer victimization in grade 5, broader than a verified bullying definition
candidates.outcome: alcohol, marijuana and tobacco use in grade 10, not SUD
candidates.text_reviewed: Complete 15-page CDC-hosted PMC author-manuscript PDF and PubMed record; text extracted with pypdf
candidates.bounded_use: A US cohort reported an indirect association between grade-5 peer victimization and grade-10 substance use through grade-7 depressive symptoms. Label the exposure peer victimization, not confirmed repeated bullying; mediation is statistical, not causal.
candidates.strength: Prospective ordering across three school grades in 4,297 youth, six-item peer-victimization measure, specified substance outcomes and attrition weighting (16.5% loss).
candidates.critical_limit: The modeled indirect paths are small and observed simple victimization–later-use correlations are near zero; do not claim a robust direct total effect. The six-item peer-victimization measure does not establish repeated bullying or power imbalance. Outcomes are any past-30-day use, not misuse or disorder; self-report, mediator confounding and limited settings remain.

candidates.title: Bullying and Substance Use in Early Adolescence: Investigating the Longitudinal and Reciprocal Effects Over 3 Years
candidates.outcome: smoking and alcohol use, not SUD
candidates.text_reviewed: Frontiers full text and PubMed record
candidates.bounded_use: In 1,495 Swiss adolescents, bullying perpetration and smoking/alcohol use covaried between persons; the pooled model's age-12 perpetration-to-age-13 use path was positive (standardized beta 0.18, p<0.05), but later and reverse paths were not significant. Never use it as victimization or SUD evidence.
candidates.strength: Three waves and random-intercept cross-lagged modeling separate between-person from within-person patterns.
candidates.critical_limit: Self-reported perpetration and combined smoking/drinking score, 95/1,495 cases excluded from the fitted model, short follow-up and possible unmeasured time-varying confounding limit causal inference. The pooled cross-lagged path was significant, but sex-stratified paths were not; the discussion's no-cross-lagged wording refers to sex-specific models and is easy to overread. The outcome is use, not disorder.

candidates.title: Cyberbullying, mental health, and substance use experimentation among early adolescents: a prospective cohort study
candidates.outcome: one-year alcohol, nicotine and cannabis experimentation, not SUD
candidates.text_reviewed: Complete PMC BioC full-text record and PubMed record
candidates.bounded_use: ABCD data show adjusted prospective associations of cyberbullying victimization with alcohol, nicotine and cannabis experimentation one year later. This is cyberbullying, not all traditional bullying, and experimentation is not disorder.
candidates.strength: Large cohort (9,799), prospective ordering, adjustment for baseline substance experimentation and measured sociodemographics, survey weights and sensitivity analysis restricted to new experimentation.
candidates.critical_limit: Exposure is a single unvalidated lifetime self-report item, so onset/repetition are unknown; experimentation is as little as one sip or puff. The 9,799 analyzed exclude participants with missing use or cyberbullying data; selection and residual confounding remain, and the ABCD sample is not independent of earlier ABCD analyses.
candidates.overlap_note: Likely shares the ABCD cohort with PMID 37598455; do not count as independent replication without wave/sample comparison.
